meta.title: Multi-Leader Replication: Write Conflicts and Resolution

segments.label: Two clients write the same key concurrently, each to their own leader
Leaders exchange the write via cross-region replication
Both clients eventually see the same converged value

cards.title: Why Multi-Leader Needs Conflict Resolution
items: Two leaders can each accept a write to the same key at nearly the same moment, with neither aware of the other
By the time they replicate to each other, both already told their own client the write succeeded
Something has to pick one outcome so every replica converges to the same value

cards.title: Common Resolution Strategies
items: Last-Write-Wins (LWW): keep the write with the latest timestamp, silently discard the other — simple, but the discarded write is gone for good
Merge: for structures like sets or counters, combine both writes instead of picking one (CRDTs)
Application-level resolution: store both versions as siblings and let the application (or the user) decide, as Amazon Dynamo originally did

cards.title: Where This Shows Up
items: Multi-region active-active databases (CockroachDB, Cassandra, Cosmos DB)
Offline-first mobile/collaborative apps that sync changes made while disconnected
Git itself: two branches editing the same line is a conflict a human has to resolve, same root problem
